attributed_victim_count.notes: 61 additional victims of 161 uncharged offences — attempted murder, kidnapping to commit robbery, rape, robbery, first-degree burglary, false imprisonment and criminal threats — admitted in open court and set out by six prosecuting agencies. This is the rare case where an attribution figure carries genuine agency provenance: it was stated by named District Attorneys in official releases, as part of a negotiated disposition, not derived from press synthesis. It is NOT a homicide count and must never be added to confirmed_victim_count.

claimed_victim_count.notes: No separate offender-claimed total distinct from the admissions recorded in the plea. Unlike USA-002-RIDGWAY, where self-report and agency attribution diverge, here the admissions were made in court and adopted by the prosecuting agencies, so they belong in attributed_victim_count.

estimate_provenance.value: The counts in this record derive entirely from the joint prosecution's own published accounting. No higher figure from press synthesis is recorded.

employment_history.notes: The single most consequential fact in this record. He joined Exeter PD in 1975 — the same year and the same county as the Snelling homicide — and was a serving officer through the early years of the offending. Compare USA-002-RIDGWAY, where the occupational fact that mattered was three decades of stable shift work. Here it is warrant card access to the institution investigating him.

detection_delay_factors.value: Thirty-two years elapsed between the final charged homicide and identification. The delay is not explained by linkage blindness: the offence series were linked to one another well before they were linked to a person, and the multiple press epithets record the successive stages of that linkage. The binding constraint was that no method existed to convert retained biological evidence into an identification when the offender was not himself in a criminal DNA database.

detection_delay_factors.notes: This case, Ridgway and Bundy give the dataset three distinct delay mechanisms: absent technology here, institutional neglect and forensic limits in Ridgway, jurisdictional fragmentation in Bundy. They should not be collapsed into a single 'linkage blindness' explanation.

identifying_evidence.value: Identified in April 2018 by investigative genetic genealogy: crime-scene DNA was compared against a public consumer genealogy database to locate distant relatives, from whom a family tree was constructed to a candidate, who was then confirmed by direct comparison.

forensic_methods_used.value: Investigative genetic genealogy (IGG), followed by direct DNA comparison for confirmation.

forensic_methods_used.notes: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION. IGG is contested on privacy and governance grounds, not on grounds of reliability. Erlich et al. (2018) showed that long-range familial search could identify a majority of individuals of European descent in the United States from third-cousin matches, and Guerrini et al. (2018) set out the consent and governance problems: the people whose data enable an identification did not upload it for that purpose and are not suspects. That is an ethical and regulatory objection. It is NOT the objection that applies to bite-mark comparison or polygraphy, which is that they do not work. Conflating the two is a category error, and this record deliberately does not place IGG in method_now_disputed.

method_now_disputed.notes: No technique relied on in this conviction has been found scientifically unreliable. The field is null by design and the reasoning is recorded in forensic_methods_used — a contested method is not the same thing as a discredited one.
